      "text": "On a cutting board, slice the cheese lengthwise, so it's between 1/2-inch and 1-inch thick. It may be in two or more smaller pieces. Sprinkle the flour evenly over a large plate. Dip the cheese in the flour, dredging until lightly coated on all sides; discard any remaining flour.",

  "notes": "Can't find halloumi? Look for other firm, slightly springy cheeses. Kasseri or kefalotyri are two popular options, but queso fresco, Manchego or paneer would work, too. Don't wear loose clothing, and keep long hair tied back. Never pour alcohol into a dish directly from the bottle as the flame can travel up into the bottle; pour the booze into a heatproof cup and then into the food.       "name": "Step 1",
      "text": "Slice the chicken breasts against the grain on the diagonal to form wide strips that are no more than 3-4mm (about \u215b inch) thick.\u00a0",

    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "Step 2",
      "text": "Whisk together the marinade ingredients in a large bowl. Add the chicken and mix well with your hands to make sure each slice gets a little love from the marinade. Set aside for 10 minutes.",
      "image": "https://www.marionskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Hoisin-Chicken-Stir-fry-01.jpg",
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "Step 3",
      "text": "To make the hoisin stir-fry sauce, mix the ingredients in a small bowl until combined.\u00a0",
      "image": "https://www.marionskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Hoisin-Chicken-Stir-fry-01.jpg",
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "Step 4",
      "text": "Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large non-stick frying pan over high heat. Add the onion and stir-fry for 30 seconds or until just starting to char. Push the onion to the sides of the pan and add the chicken and marinade into the centre. Spread the chicken out as much as possible and leave for about 3\u20134 minutes, or until a crust begins to form. Then combine with the other ingredients in the wok. ",
      "image": "https://www.marionskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/06/Hoisin-Chicken-Stir-fry-01.jpg",
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": "Step 5",
      "text": "Toss through the garlic. Then add the capsicum. Stir-fry for another 30 seconds until fragrant. Toss through the spring onion. Serve immediately.",

  "recipeInstructions": [
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 1,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Let's start first with the enchilada sauce. Slightly roast the peppers in a hot griddle, pressing them flat with the help of a spatula. Make sure NOT to burn them. This step takes a few seconds on each side of the peppers.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 2,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Once roasted, place them in a saucepan with water and turn the heat to medium and simmer for about 15 minutes or when they look soft.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 3,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Remove saucepan from stove and let them cool for another 10-15 minutes. The pepper skins should look soft.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 4,
      "name": "",
      "text": "After the resting period, drain the peppers and place in the blender along with the garlic cloves. Add 1/2 cup of clean water and blend until you have a smooth sauce. If necessary, strain the sauce into a large bowl using a fine strainer. Season with the oregano, salt, and pepper, and set aside.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 5,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Preheat your oven to 350 degrees, just to keep the red enchiladas warm while you finish assembling them. Add the 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add oil little by little as needed. To much oil will get a soggy tortilla.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 6,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Dip the tortilla into the enchilada sauce to lightly coat each side.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 7,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Place it in the Frying Comal-pan  or skillet and briefly fry a few seconds on both sides. Add more vegetable oil to the skillet as needed.  Place fried tortillas in a dish while you make the rest of the tortillas to keep warm in the oven.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 8,
      "name": "",
      "text": "To assemble the red enchiladas, first, place the filling in the center of the tortilla and fold it. Sometimes I place a meat filling into the center of the tortilla and then roll it, like in the pictures above.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 9,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Sprinkle the enchiladas with the cheese and onion. Add the garnish of your choice and enjoy!",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 10,
      "name": "",
      "text": "If you decide to add the potatoes and carrots as a garnish: Peel potatoes and carrots, cut into cubes and boil until almost tender but still firm. Then drain and cool.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    },
    {
      "@type": "HowToStep",
      "position": 11,
      "name": "",
      "text": "Use the same frying pan where you fried the red enchiladas to lightly fry the potatoes, adding a little more oil. The potatoes and carrots will be coated with some of the sauce sticking to the frying pan. Season with salt and garnish with cheese.",
      "image": null,
      "imageCredit": null
    }
